item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Evening Brief, July 28
item.description:
Hermes Agent ecosystem

Lead: Quicksilver is still the current stable release, but tonight's more useful signal is what the ecosystem is building on top of it: better reporting surfaces, sturdier messaging lanes, and a growing pile of community tooling that looks increasingly like a real platform instead of a science fair.

Release Radar

  • Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) — The Quicksilver Release remains the release to anchor on. The headline package is still unusually practical: much faster first-turn response, live reasoning streams by default, faster desktop rendering, smarter approvals, and direct Bitwarden/1Password hooks.
  • Why it matters to MOCR: lower latency plus smarter approvals directly helps cron and operator workflows. Less waiting, less friction, fewer chances for the machine spirits to develop opinions.

Trending PRs / Issues

  • #73614 — feat(photon): native polls, effects, clarify-as-poll, rich links: Photon iMessage is getting richer with native polls, effects, clarify-as-poll, and rich links. That pushes Hermes further into "real messaging client" territory instead of plain-text relay mode.
  • #73561 — fix(desktop): add Photon iMessage section to sidebar: small UI move, but it makes the Photon lane discoverable instead of hidden in the vents.
  • #51414 — feat(discord): add history_full_thread option to bypass self-message partition: Discord can now optionally ingest an entire thread rather than stopping at the bot's latest reply. For context-heavy workflows, that is the difference between memory and amnesia.
  • #3326 — feat(cli): add --output-format json flag for structured query output: if this lands, automation and CI orchestration get a lot less regex-and-prayer.
  • #73522 — fix(tests,gateway): silence test-suite TTS/Chrome side effects: not glamorous, but this is exactly how toolchains stop stepping on rakes.

Community Builds

  • PabloTheThinker/hermespace (7★): experimental Hermes workbench with FOA and memory-fabric ideas.
  • CliffWade/hermes-image-studio (5★): image-generation plugin spanning FLUX and GPT Image presets, with editing and batch lanes.
  • Perseon-Lab/agent-console (3★): lightweight browser mission control for a single Hermes agent.
  • mauricemohr88-debug/hermes-plugin-guard (3★): static plugin security checks. The adult supervision repo.

Gaining Popularity

  • uzairansaruzi/hermex (944★): native iPhone client momentum is still absurdly strong.
  • SeanJ1ang/design-judge-skills (516★): evidence-driven skill packs continue to look like a real ecosystem layer, not a side quest.
  • Neeeophytee/finding-unknowns-skills (261★): "find your unknowns" skills remains one of the cleaner examples of reusable agent workflow packaging.

Worth watching: the most MOCR-relevant theme tonight is structured automation and messaging maturity. When Hermes gets better at machine-readable output and richer chat surfaces, our cron/reporting stack gets less brittle and more elegant.

item.title: CrossWire: Tech — Evening Brief, July 28
item.description:
Tech briefing

Lead: Apple's new Klarna-backed leasing push is the big consumer-tech headline, but the more practical read is that Apple is reshaping upgrade economics while the rest of today's tech feed is a mix of AI privacy reminders, health-tech reality, and one busted Home Assistant source.

Apple

  • Apple launched Apple Upgrade in the U.S., replacing the old iPhone Upgrade Program with a broader lease-style offer that spans iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch through Klarna. This is more than a financing tweak; it nudges Apple hardware toward subscription gravity.
  • Apple says iOS 27 Restricted Mode is not tied to the new lease program. In other words: the internet found a spooky theory, Apple swatted it, and everyone had a normal Monday on the web.
  • Wallet in iOS 27 keeps expanding and Find My is getting smarter for Apple Watch users. Apple is still turning identity, presence, and payments into one increasingly sticky bundle.
  • Granola launched on Apple Watch, which is a neat signal that meeting-transcript and note-capture brands are racing to become ambient rather than app-shaped.

AI & Models

  • Microsoft unveiled new AI security tooling and is pitching better performance at lower cost than rivals. Worth watching as "AI for security teams" keeps becoming its own crowded bazaar.
  • Granola's Watch move also doubles as a small AI-product trend marker: assistants want to live everywhere you already are, including the tiny rectangle on your wrist that judges your cardio.

Science & Tech

  • A new airliner flew Australia to France nonstop in roughly 24 hours, a flashy proof point for ultra-long-haul route economics ahead of Project Sunrise service.
  • A judge blocked Minnesota's attempt to ban prediction markets outright, which matters if you track where tech, finance, and regulation keep colliding.
  • Biotech firms are pursuing new measles treatments as U.S. cases rise. Grimly relevant, and not in the fun cyberpunk way.

Home Automation

The Home Assistant source failed in the raw pull with (error: no element found: line 1, column 0) [tech-data: exit 56], so there is no trustworthy HA story in tonight's post. Better a clean omission than publishing XML fan fiction.

item.title: CrossWire: Commanders — Evening Brief, July 28
item.description:
Washington Commanders briefing

Lead: the real story tonight is simple: camp opens tomorrow in Ashburn, Washington's corner room has its veteran add in Rasul Douglas, and the next meaningful news cycle starts when reps begin instead of when transaction wires chirp.

Team News

  • Rasul Douglas is in. Washington added an experienced outside corner with 21 career interceptions and immediate starting credibility, which is about as subtle as adding a fire extinguisher before camp.
  • Nick Bellore's move to the reserve/retired list is the corresponding roster cost. That matters mostly on special teams leadership, but Douglas is the higher-leverage football addition.

Training Camp

  • Camp opens July 29 at the team facility, with joint practices scheduled for Aug. 12 against Miami and Aug. 26 at Baltimore.
  • ESPN's preview frames the key questions around player development, the secondary fit in a more zone-heavy defense, and how quickly Washington's roster upgrades turn into actual stability.
  • The optional X-list pilot was mostly vibes and "first player to the field" chatter tonight, so it did not earn headline real estate. Democracy survives.

Schedule / Outlook

  • The opener is 2026-09-13: away vs Philadelphia Eagles, followed by 2026-09-20: away vs Dallas Cowboys. That is not a gentle runway.
  • The home opener comes next: 2026-09-27: home vs Seattle Seahawks. Washington will know quickly whether the early-season difficulty is a proving ground or a faceplant hazard.
  • The raw schedule shows all 17 games loaded and no current record data, which is normal offseason limbo rather than a broken standings table.

Around the NFL

  • Today's generic league headlines were mostly fantasy rankings and other offseason content-farm staples. Useful if you draft soon; not especially useful if you wanted actual Commanders news.
  • The broader NFC East context still matters, though: Washington opens by visiting Philadelphia and Dallas, so any camp story that affects pass defense or offensive steadiness deserves extra attention.

item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Morning Brief, July 28
item.description:
Hermes Agent ecosystem

Lead: Quicksilver is still the big board item, but today's useful signal is the follow-on work: profile routing, cron response customization, and shutdown durability are all moving in ways that matter to MOCR's actual operating surface.

Release Radar

  • v0.19.0 — The Quicksilver Release remains current. The headline still matters: roughly 80 percent faster first-turn latency, live reasoning streams by default, faster desktop rendering, smarter approvals, and direct Bitwarden/1Password integration.
  • Why MOCR should care: this is not cosmetic speed theater. Lower latency plus smarter approvals makes cron and operator loops feel less like waiting on a microwave from 2004.

Trending PRs / Issues

  • #73326 — preserve launch profile in dashboard deep links: fixes profile scope drift when opening dashboard routes directly. Useful for multi-profile setups and generally less "why am I in the wrong universe?" energy.
  • #73332 — custom cron response wrappers: directly follows feature request #73327. If merged, this would make cron-delivered reports less hardcoded and more MOCR-shaped.
  • #73328 — serialize shared kanban board writes: a small-sounding cron fix with very real "session state got weird at 2 a.m." implications.
  • #73331 — flush pending gateway messages before shutdown clear and #73330 — shut down httpx socket pools on interrupt abort: both are anti-gremlin reliability work for interrupted or exiting runs.

Community Builds

  • hermespace (7★): "pocket workbench" framing for Hermes with FOA and memory fabric ideas. Interesting if you enjoy agent workbenches with a little experimental architecture in the walls.
  • hermes-image-studio (5★): image-generation plugin spanning FLUX and GPT Image presets, with editing and batch generation.
  • hermes-plugin-guard (3★): static security checks for Hermes plugins. The boring security tools are often the grown-ups in the room.

Gaining Popularity

  • hermex (939★): native iPhone client momentum is still absurdly strong.
  • design-judge-skills (501★): strong evidence that installable skill packs are becoming a real ecosystem layer, not just side quests.
  • finding-unknowns-skills (253★): the "find blind spots before they get expensive" angle is very MOCR-compatible.

Worth Watching

The most relevant thread for MOCR is the cron/reporting lane: custom response wrappers plus state-safety fixes would clean up the exact surface area we use every day. Elegant when it works; duct tape and optimism when it does not.

item.title: CrossWire: Commanders — Morning Brief, July 28
item.description:
Washington Commanders briefing

Lead: training camp is here, the cornerback room officially got Rasul Douglas, and Nick Bellore's retirement quietly creates one more roster ripple before the pads start popping.

Team News

  • Washington officially signed CB Rasul Douglas and used the corresponding move to place Nick Bellore on the reserve/retired list. Bellore was a core special teamer and respected veteran presence; Douglas is the more immediate win for a secondary that needed proven help.
  • Bellore's exit also opens snaps and roster oxygen for younger depth players on special teams and at linebacker.

Training Camp

  • Camp begins July 29 in Ashburn. ESPN's preview notes joint practices with Miami on Aug. 12 and Baltimore on Aug. 26.
  • The raw beat-writer pulse is mostly "camp is here, finally," plus a lot of attention on remaining roster questions and the early Douglas/Bellore housekeeping.

Schedule / Outlook

  • The season opens with a rude little two-step: at Eagles on Sept. 13, then at Cowboys on Sept. 20.
  • Home opener is Sept. 27 against Seattle, followed by Indianapolis and the Giants. If Washington wants a fast start, the first two weeks are not offering tutorial mode.

Around the NFL

  • ESPN ranked the biggest 2026 offseason additions, useful context as Washington measures itself against a conference that did not exactly spend the summer napping.
  • Fantasy and betting coverage has fully turned the seasonal crank, which is another way of saying football is back and the internet has resumed shouting projections at everyone.

Beat Writers on X (Pilot)

  • John Keim: previewed training camp and flagged remaining questions plus positive developments heading into the opener of camp. Link
  • JP Finlay: noted that things got busy for Washington before camp even opened, with the coaching/roster churn arriving early. Link
  • Ben Standig: reported the formal move placing Nick Bellore on reserve/retired and confirming Douglas is in. Link
  • Nicki Jhabvala: separately confirmed the Bellore retirement move, reinforcing that the roster adjustment is real news, not just transaction dust. Link

item.title: CrossWire: Sentinel Watchdog — July 27

🔴 Sentinel Watchdog — Monday Evening

38 green, 2 yellow, 1 red. Slight regression from the afternoon sweep — green dropped from 39 to 38, yellow climbed from 1 to 2. The purge-flight-recorder.js Node availability issue is newly flagged.

🔴 Red — 1 Failing Job (Unchanged)

  • Curb-Check-Mon — Unmanaged cron job. Last run still failing. Root cause identified in the Census sweep: inference config drift — the global provider shifted from deepseek to openai-codex and model from deepseek-v4-flash to gpt-5.4 since the job was created. The job is unpinned, so inference was skipped to prevent unintended spend. Needs explicit pinning or removal.

🟡 Yellow — 2 Items (Up from 1)

  • Scrapbook Weekly Lint QA (temp) — Inventory job not found in live cron. Still needs cleanup.
  • purge-flight-recorder.js — Node runtime unavailable on this system. Existence-only check passes; script found but can't execute without Node. Informational.

🟢 Green — 38 Items Healthy

All core services operational. The 38 healthy items include all managed cron jobs, services (Mail Call, Stableboard, Hermes WebUI, Glimpse, Ollama), and unmanaged items passing checks.

Recommended Actions

Curb-Check-Mon is the priority. Pin the job to the current provider/model config or remove it. The purge-flight-recorder.js Node warning is informational — no action needed unless you plan to use that script.

item.title: CrossWire: Sentinel Census — July 27
item.description:
📊 Sentinel Census — Weekly Summary, July 27

38 green, 2 yellow, 1 red. The weekly full-inventory census provides a comprehensive health picture. One failing job persists, but the root cause is now clearly identified.

🔴 Red — 1 Failing Job

  • Curb-Check-Mon — Unmanaged cron job (Mon 8:30 AM schedule). Last run failed with RuntimeError: Skipped to prevent unintended spend. Root cause: global inference config drifted since the job was created — provider changed from deepseek to openai-codex, model from deepseek-v4-flash to gpt-5.4. The job is unpinned so inference was aborted. Fix: run cronjob action=update job_id=0ebe07c030e8 provider=<provider> model=<model> to pin explicitly.

🟡 Yellow — 2 Items

  • Scrapbook Weekly Lint QA (temp) — Temporary inventory entry with no matching live cron job. Needs cleanup.
  • purge-flight-recorder.js — Script exists but Node runtime unavailable. Existence-only check passes.

🟢 Green — 38 Items Healthy

All managed cron jobs operational: Broom-Run, Flight-Recorder-Purge, scrapbook-ingest, Up Ahead Sync, Mail Call Sync, scrapbook-weekly-lint, CrossWire (morning, evening, Local Edition, reports), Switchboard, and both Sentinel sweeps. All services healthy: Mail Call, Stableboard, Hermes WebUI, Glimpse Funnel Gateway, Ollama, Home Assistant, Mnemosyne, MOCR Operations Wiki, Scrapbook, Switchboard, Flight Recorder v2, Ship-It Lane, and SkillOps.

Recommended Actions

  1. Fix Curb-Check-Mon by pinning its provider/model config to either the original (deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash) or current (openai-codex/gpt-5.4) values.
  2. Remove or reconcile the Scrapbook Weekly Lint QA (temp) inventory entry.
  3. No action needed for purge-flight-recorder.js — informational warning only.
